column1: # VOCABULARY. Values recovered from these markers are OBSERVED - a camera
# actually saw them. That is the one approved exception to the rule against
# "measured". Nothing here observes a servo output shaft directly; it observes
# the printed part the shaft is bolted to.
# SIZE COLUMNS.
#   black_square_mm       edge of the ArUco black square - the number you pass
#                         to cv2.aruco / solvePnP as the marker length.
#   approximate_size_mm   edge of the whole printed sticker INCLUDING the white
#                         quiet zone - the number you cut out. It is
#                         black_square_mm * 8/6 for DICT_4X4_50 (6 modules of
#                         marker + 1 module of quiet zone each side).
#   Sizing rule actually applied:
#       black_square_mm = floor((measured_inscribed_square_mm - 2.0) / 1.3333)
#   The 2.0 mm is application margin for a hand-placed sticker.
# GRADE COLUMNS - READ THESE TOGETHER. grade_at_design_standoff is meaningless
# without design_standoff_mm; a marker that is below-floor on the overview
# camera can be pose-grade on the close camera. The grade vocabulary is exactly
# three values and nothing else:
#   pose         projected black square >= 36 px - stable 6-DOF pose
#   detect       projected black square >= 24 px - detected; pose is unstable
#   below-floor  projected black square <  24 px - NOT DETECTED at all
# Grades are computed as projected_px = 1108 * black_square_mm * 0.7 /
# design_standoff_mm

A 20 mm sticker spans about 19 deg of arc - about 0.8 mm of bow - so use centroid and azimuth only; do NOT trust single-tag pose here. Preferred fix is a flat printed tab - MARKER-SYSTEM.md section 8.

column8: J1 pitches about a horizontal sideways axis; this face normal is PARALLEL to that axis so the marker rotates IN-PLANE across the whole 0-91 deg range and never tilts away. 23.99 px at the design standoff - it MISSES the 24 px detection floor by a hundredth of a pixel. That is not a margin in either direction: it crosses at about 549 mm. Treat the shoulder as unobservable on CAM-A and fix it properly via MARKER-SYSTEM.md section 8. Do NOT use the x=-22.5 or x=+22.5 rails: they look ideal at fill 1.00 but they are inner walls of a channel with material outboard of them.

column4: Same y=+15 broad side face - the second solid island 176.6 mm away along the link.
column6: Survey second-square centre - near the far end of the 231.8 mm face from SHOULDER-1.
column8: BASELINE MARKER - 176.6 mm is the longest baseline anywhere on this arm and gives the best angle resolution in the set (about 0.035 deg at 0.2 px centroid noise and 600 mm standoff). Both markers are on ONE part so that baseline is real and not an assembly guess. But the solid island here is only 13.6 mm so the marker is 8 mm and it is BELOW the detection floor on the overview camera. Usable only closer than about 260 mm or with the flat-tab upgrade.

J4 is also the joint whose 0-180 limits are flagged SUSPECT in joint-limits.csv - the travel this marker must cover may not all be physically reachable.
